prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: نتائج الانتخابات حسب الدائرة (language ar, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 5 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "الدائرة" spans 1 col × 2 row; "المرشح أ" spans 2 col × 1 row; "المرشح ب" spans 2 col × 1 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 17px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "الدائرة" · longest unbreakable word 49px · one-line width 130px
  col 2: header "المرشح أ › الأصوات" · longest unbreakable word 58px · one-line width 58px
  col 3: header "المرشح أ › النسبة" · longest unbreakable word 50px · one-line width 50px
  col 4: header "المرشح ب › الأصوات" · longest unbreakable word 58px · one-line width 58px
  col 5: header "المرشح ب › النسبة" · longest unbreakable word 50px · one-line width 50px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 413px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 412px.
Fixed: content, font, 17px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 413px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Publication table of election results by district, comparing candidate A and candidate B vote counts and vote shares in each district.","reading":"Right-to-left: identify the district at the far right, then scan candidate A votes and percentage, then candidate B votes and percentage; compare candidates within each row and compare vote/share columns down the table.","groups":["col 1: row identifier (district)","cols 2–3: candidate A block (votes, percentage)","cols 4–5: candidate B block (votes, percentage)","cols 2 and 4: vote counts, same role and should align","cols 3 and 5: percentages, same role and should align"],"keep_intact":["all vote counts such as 21,340 and 13,905","all percentages such as 41.2% and 8.6%","candidate labels المرشح أ and المرشح ب","unbreakable Arabic words in district names"],"may_wrap":["multi-word district names such as دائرة المفرق الأولى","two-level header labels if necessary, but not numeric data cells"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[112,79,71,79,71],"idea":"District-priority: give the row label the largest possible width while keeping every numeric column exactly at its one-line minimum."},{"name":"B","widths":[98,86,71,86,71],"idea":"Vote-comfort: trade district width for extra breathing room in the two vote columns, while percentages stay at their intact minimum."},{"name":"C","widths":[84,82,82,82,82],"idea":"Numeric symmetry: make all four numeric columns equal and generous, accepting a compact district column that wraps row labels more aggressively."}]}
